loading.tip.1: Mercs who are tired, drunk or wounded shoot worse. Rest them on the map screen before a big fight.
loading.tip.2: Crouching or lying prone makes a merc harder to hit and steadies their aim.
loading.tip.3: Aiming costs action points but raises the chance to hit. Right-click with the target cursor to aim more.
loading.tip.4: Train militia in towns you hold, or the Queen's army will take them back.
loading.tip.5: A merc with a medical kit can bandage the wounded in combat; doctors heal them faster between fights.
loading.tip.6: Bleeding mercs lose health every turn. Bandage them before they pass out.
loading.tip.7: Repair kits and a merc on the repair assignment keep your weapons and armour in shape.
loading.tip.8: Night fighting favours those who can see: night-vision goggles and mercs with the night ops skill.
loading.tip.9: Doors can be locked or trapped. Check them before you open them.
loading.tip.10: Mines pay a daily income once you hold them and the miners trust you.
loading.tip.11: Town loyalty rises when you free a town and falls when civilians get hurt.
loading.tip.12: Headshots do more damage but are harder to land.
loading.tip.13: Throwing a grenade over a wall reaches enemies you cannot see. Mind the bounce.
loading.tip.14: Keep an eye on your mercs' contracts: a merc whose contract runs out simply leaves.
loading.tip.15: Mercs gain experience by doing: shooting raises marksmanship, healing raises medical.
loading.tip.16: Enemies hear gunfire. A silenced weapon or a knife keeps a fight quiet.
loading.tip.17: Save before you enter an enemy sector. Iron Man only lets you save outside combat.
loading.tip.18: Bobby Ray's delivers to Drassen's airport once you hold it.
loading.tip.19: The helicopter needs a pilot and fuel, and it cannot fly through SAM site cover.
loading.tip.20: Some mercs refuse to work with people they dislike. Check their files before hiring.
loading.tip.21: Leadership helps when training militia; wisdom helps a merc learn.
loading.tip.22: Breath runs low when a merc runs, climbs or is hit. A merc out of breath cannot act well.
loading.tip.23: Burst fire uses more ammunition but hits more often at short range.
loading.tip.24: Explosives and a merc with explosives skill open doors that keys cannot.
loading.tip.25: Talk to the locals. Some have work for you, some have information, some have both.
loading.tip.26: A merc on patrol in a sector with militia can spot enemies coming.
loading.tip.27: Dropping a heavy pack lets a merc move and breathe more easily in a long fight.
loading.tip.28: Hospitals and a good doctor turn a long convalescence into a short one.
loading.tip.29: Look at the sector inventory: enemies leave their gear behind.
loading.tip.30: Attachments such as scopes and bipods make a good weapon better.
loading.tip.31: Move in short hops from cover to cover when the enemy has the high ground.
loading.tip.32: Climbing onto roofs gives a wide view, and makes you a target.
loading.tip.33: Money is short early on. Take the mines before you hire a big team.
loading.tip.34: Stealthy movement is slower but much quieter.
loading.tip.35: The Queen's army grows stronger the longer you take. Keep moving.
loading.tip.36: Squads travel faster by road, and much faster by car or helicopter.
loading.tip.37: Traps and mines hurt everyone. Watch where you walk.
loading.tip.38: Mercs on the doctor assignment need a medical kit to work.
loading.tip.39: Interrupts let alert mercs act during the enemy's turn. Keep action points for them.
loading.tip.40: Dead is Dead has one save. Every decision counts.
